title: Running Median Sum
statement:
Numbers arrive one at a time in `stream`. After each number arrives, find the **median** of all numbers received so far: the middle value when they are sorted. When an even amount has arrived there are two middle values: use the **smaller** of the two.

Return the sum of all these medians (one per arrival).

hints.nudge: The median only depends on the middle of the sorted numbers. Do you need the whole sorted list, or just the two halves around the middle?
hints.pattern: Two heaps: a max-heap for the smaller half of the numbers and a min-heap for the larger half. The median sits at the top of the smaller half.
hints.pseudocode:
low = max-heap, high = min-heap
for each x:
  if low is not empty and x > top of low: push x on high else push x on low
  if low has 2 more items than high: move the top of low to high
  else if high has more items than low: move the top of high to low
  total += top of low
return total
hints.walkthrough: Sorting all numbers seen so far after every arrival costs O(n^2 log n). Instead split the numbers into a smaller half and a larger half. The smaller half lives in a max-heap `low` (its top is the largest of the small numbers), the larger half in a min-heap `high` (its top is the smallest of the large numbers). Keep `low` the same size as `high`, or one bigger. Then the smaller of the two middle values (or the one middle value) is exactly the top of `low`. A new number goes to the half it belongs to; afterwards, if the sizes are off by too much, move one top element across. Each arrival costs O(log n), so O(n log n) in total. In languages with only a min-heap, store negated numbers for the max-heap. Use a 64-bit sum.
